text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help diagnose the newborn's jaundice, could you please tell me the baby's exact age in hours and whether the yellowing started in the first 24 hours of life?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-week-old female newborn. The patient has been experiencing increasing yellow discoloration of her eyes and skin for 2 days. She was born at 39 weeks' gestation, initially weighed 3066 g and now weighs 3200 g. The patient is exclusively breastfed.

speaker: Doctor
text: Is the baby having at least six wet diapers and three stools per day, and are the stools yellow and seedy rather than pale or clay-colored? Also, has there been any family history of jaundice or blood disorders?

text: The lab results show predominantly unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia with normal liver enzymes, which makes biliary atresia unlikely. Given the family history and the baby's age, I need to rule out hemolysis. REQUEST TEST: Blood_Type_and_Coombs_Test, Reticulocyte_Count

speaker: Doctor
text: With hemolysis and liver disease ruled out, this presentation is consistent with breast milk jaundice. I will confirm the absence of thyroid dysfunction, which can also cause prolonged jaundice. REQUEST TEST: TSH, Free_T4
